cluster_name.description: Name of the cluster — must be identical on all nodes and DNS-compatible

dc_deadtime.description: Time in seconds after which a node is considered dead if unresponsive (affects DC election stability)

start_standby.description: If true, nodes start in standby mode and do not host resources until explicitly enabled

stonith_enabled.description: Enable STONITH/fencing to prevent split-brain; required for production clusters

no_quorum_policy.description: Action to take when cluster loses quorum (majority of nodes). Options: 'stop', 'freeze', 'ignore', 'suicide'

resource_defaults.description: Global fallback values for resource operations and failure handling

migration_threshold.description: How many failures before resource is migrated to another node (0 = never migrate automatically)

op_timeout.description: Default timeout (in seconds) for resource operations (start/stop/monitor)

interval_origin.description: Offset (in seconds) to add to monitoring intervals to stagger operations across nodes

resource_failure_stickiness.description: Score penalty applied to the node where a resource fails; 'INFINITY' prevents re-migration until manually fixed

location_constraints.description: Constraints defining where specific resources should or must run (e.g., prefer a node, or rule-out others)

resource.description: Name of the primitive/group/clone to constrain

score.description: Preference score: 'INFINITY', positive integer (higher = preferred), or negative (avoid)

node.description: Name of the node to apply the score to

colocation_constraints.description: Constraints that keep resources together on the same node (e.g., IP + Apache)

score.description: Colocation strength: 'INFINITY', 'INFINITY-100', or a positive/negative integer

resources.description: List of resource IDs to colocate (order matters: last item is primary)

ordering_constraints.description: Constraints that enforce resource startup/shutdown order (e.g., IP must start before web server)

resources.description: Resource IDs in order of startup (left to right)
List of primitives (un-grouped resources) to manage (IP, filesystems, services, etc.)

op_defaults.description: Custom operation settings for this resource (e.g., 'monitor interval=10s')

params.description: Resource parameters (key=value) required by the agent

groups.description: Logical groupings of primitives to colocate and order together (e.g., web server + VIP)

members.description: List of resource IDs to include in the group (must exist)

clones.description: Clone definitions for stateful resources that run on multiple nodes (e.g., DLM, gfs2, STONITH)

resource.description: Name of the resource to clone (must be a primitive or group)

globally_unique.description: If false, clones may run multiple instances per node (rarely needed)

op_defaults.description: Default monitoring operation parameters for all resources
